signature.name: Rheinturm
signature.detail: Düsseldorf's most famous landmark, a slender concrete television tower on the Rhine with an observation deck and restaurant offering sweeping views over the city and river. Go near sunset for the best light, and check opening hours before you climb since the deck can close early in winter.

signature.name: Altstadt, Düsseldorf
signature.detail: The historic old town, known as the 'longest bar in the world' for its dense cluster of pubs and breweries, is the heart of the city and a must for a first visit. Wander it on foot in the late afternoon, then settle in for an evening of Altbier.

signature.name: Königsallee
signature.detail: Düsseldorf's grand boulevard, split by a wide canal lined with trees and high-end shops, is the city's elegant showcase. It is free to stroll; come on a weekday morning for a quieter walk and good photos along the water.

signature.name: Schloss Benrath
signature.detail: A pink rococo palace set in parkland on the southern edge of the city, one of Düsseldorf's finest historic sights. Reach it by tram or S-Bahn, and book a guided interior tour in advance as access is by tour only.

signature.name: St. Lambertus Basilica
signature.detail: The old town's landmark church with its distinctive twisted spire, a short walk from the Rhine promenade. Entry is free and quiet; visit in the morning to avoid crowds and dress respectfully.

food: Casual meal $12-20; brewery plate with Altbier around $15
transport: Tram or U-Bahn single ticket about $3; day pass good value
